name: accordion
purpose: Vertically stacked headings that each show or hide a section of content (WAI-ARIA APG Accordion), built on native headings and buttons, with single or multiple expansion and an animated height transition.
whenToUse: Long pages where users need only some sections at a time, such as FAQs or settings groups.
Progressive disclosure of secondary details in a constrained space.
whenNotToUse: Content users must read or compare side by side: show it on the page.
Switching between peer views of the same content: use Tabs.
A single show/hide toggle: a native <details> element is enough.
Navigation menus: use a navigation component.
responsive: Full width of its container. Headers wrap long titles (overflow-wrap: anywhere); the indicator icon stays at the inline end.
rtl: Logical properties: the title sits at the inline start and the indicator at the inline end in both directions.
theme: Border, text, muted-text, hover, and focus-ring role tokens. Forced-colors mode uses CanvasText borders and a Highlight focus outline.
security: Titles and string content are rendered with textContent; never parsed as HTML. Node content is inserted as-is and is the consumer's responsibility. CSP-safe.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry.

performance.testedScale: Unit-tested with up to 7 items; designed for tens of items.

limitations: Collapsed panel content is removed from the find-in-page index (hidden attribute); hidden=until-found is not used.
The icon rotation and height transition are removed under reduced motion or animation 'none'; the rotated end state remains as a static indicator.
Changing `items` re-creates the item DOM; Node content is moved, not cloned.
unsupported: Rendering HTML strings as titles or content (pass a Node for rich content).
antiPatterns: Hiding content users need to complete a task.
Putting form fields that may hold errors in collapsed panels without expanding them on validation.
Using heading levels that skip the page outline; set headingLevel to match the surrounding headings.
